label: Heavy going
summary: The world holds at 38, still in the 'Bad' band, as the Gulf war acquires a second front and Latin America absorbs a bad night of weather and geology. Yemen's Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia on an 'eye for an eye' rationale, drawing condemnation from Riyadh, which promised 'all necessary measures'; roughly 4 million barrels a day move from Yanbu through Bab al-Mandeb, and analysts warned that a blockade layered on top of the Strait of Hormuz disruption could put a quarter of world oil and gas supply at risk. The US bombed Iran for a tenth consecutive night, with strikes reported near Sirak and Isfahan, Iran hitting American assets in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait, three tankers ablaze in Hormuz and the US military death toll reaching at least 17; the one genuinely hopeful thread was a mediators' proposal for a 10-day ceasefire, the first concrete diplomacy since the June memorandum collapsed. An Israeli drone strike killed an entire family of six in Gaza City's Sabra neighbourhood, and Hamas named Khalil al-Hayya its new leader. Russia sent 58 drones into Ukraine overnight, hitting a shopping centre in Sumy, a recruitment centre in Chernihiv, a cargo ship at Mykolaiv and port infrastructure at Odesa and Chornomorsk. DR Congo's Ebola outbreak accelerated to 930 deaths and more than 2,300 confirmed cases, with the WHO warning it is spreading faster than previous outbreaks. Chile declared a state of catastrophe after storms flooded Coquimbo and Huasco, leaving about five dead and nearly 100,000 people isolated, and a magnitude 5.1 quake in Peru's Junin region killed six. President Trump invoked a statute dormant for seventy years to put 50 percent tariffs on some 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods, which Prime Minister Carney called a direct violation of the USMCA. The brighter column was real if narrow: Wall Street rallied on semiconductors, astronomers confirmed the first atmosphere on a rocky planet in another star's habitable zone, Pacific climate ministers met in Sydney, and solar has just become the EU's largest single power source. The headline matches the rubric formula exactly with no editorial adjustment.

drivers.headline: Yemen's Houthis declare a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia on an 'eye for an eye' rationale, accusing the kingdom of a twelve-year siege on Yemen; Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemns the move and says it will take 'all necessary measures' to safeguard its vessels, having already struck what it called Houthi military facilities at Hodeidah port. Roughly 4 million barrels a day have been shipped from Yanbu through Bab al-Mandeb in recent weeks, and analysts warn that combined with the Strait of Hormuz disruption a closure could restrict about a quarter of world oil and gas supply, with China, South Korea, Japan and India the most exposed buyers of Saudi crude

The United States bombs Iran for a tenth consecutive night, with strikes reported in several cities including Sirak and Isfahan, while Iran retaliates against American assets in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait and at least three oil tankers catch fire in the Strait of Hormuz; the US military death toll reaches at least 17 service members, among them 19-year-old Private Isabella Gonzales and First Lieutenant Tyler James Feehan, and the Pentagon is reported to have withheld nearly 100 troop injuries. Regional mediators have put a proposed 10-day ceasefire to Washington and Tehran, the first concrete diplomacy since the June memorandum of understanding collapsed

An Israeli drone strike kills an entire Palestinian family of six in the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City without warning: Firas al-Masri, his wife Salsabeel, their three daughters and their son. The strike lands as Hamas selects Khalil al-Hayya, who survived an Israeli assassination attempt in Doha that killed his son, as its new leader, filling the vacancy left by Yahya Sinwar

Russian forces attack Ukraine with 58 drones overnight into July 21, with impacts recorded across Sumy, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, Odesa, Mykolaiv, Chernihiv and Poltava regions; strikes hit an Epicenter shopping centre in Sumy, a territorial recruitment centre building in Chernihiv, a dry cargo ship in the port of Mykolaiv and port infrastructure at Odesa and Chornomorsk, as Russia claims small gains around Ulanovo and in the Vovchansk direction

The death toll from DR Congo's Ebola outbreak surges to 930 with more than 2,300 confirmed cases, and the World Health Organization warns the outbreak is spreading faster than previous ones; in neighbouring Kenya, protests against a US-backed quarantine facility turn violent and leave two people dead

President Trump imposes 50 percent tariffs on a slate of Canadian goods ranging from wine to hockey sticks to cement, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 for the first time in roughly seventy years and hitting products covered by the USMCA free-trade agreement; energy, potash, fish and critical minerals are exempted, the duties take effect in 30 days, and Prime Minister Mark Carney calls the move 'a direct violation' of the treaty while saying Canada is ready to intensify discussions

Chile declares a state of catastrophe after a frontal storm system floods the Coquimbo and Huasco areas, killing about five people, affecting roughly 2,200 more, leaving nearly 100,000 isolated and damaging some 35 homes as schools suspend classes; the same day a magnitude 5.1 earthquake in Peru's Junin region kills six people and affects more than 300 residents, while Brazil's government holds emergency meetings over new US tariffs and Rio state removes an infrastructure official amid an 86-million-real graft investigation

Tens of thousands of youth-led protesters rally against Prime Minister Modi's government in India, demanding the education minister's resignation over a national exam paper leak that forced millions of students to sit a retest; some students have died by suicide, and the police crackdown on the weeks-long demonstrations draws sharp criticism

Oil stays elevated on war risk: Brent slips 35 cents, or 0.4 percent, to 88.87 dollars a barrel and WTI holds at 82.47 dollars, close to a more-than-one-month high, after a tanker is struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz northeast of Oman's Limah and the Houthis announce a ban on maritime traffic linked to Saudi Arabia; the proposed 10-day ceasefire is the only factor capping the gain

Wall Street rallies despite the tariff and war headlines, with the Nasdaq climbing 1.00 percent to 25,373.85, the S&P 500 adding 0.70 percent to 7,489.72 and the Dow rising 276.97 points, or 0.53 percent, to 52,485.03; semiconductor names lead ahead of Big Tech earnings, with Nvidia up nearly 2 percent after announcing an investment in cloud provider Nebius

Astronomers confirm the first atmosphere ever detected around a rocky planet in another star's habitable zone: LHS 1140 b, a super-Earth some 48 light-years away orbiting a red dwarf, betrays its atmosphere through helium slowly escaping into space, detected with the WINERED spectrograph at the Magellan Observatory in Chile. The Harvard-led team under Collin Cherubim concludes the atmosphere has survived more than three billion years, closing a long-standing gap between finding well-placed rocky worlds and knowing whether any could hold on to air

The sixth Pacific Climate Ministers Talanoa convenes in Sydney, advancing regional work on holding warming to 1.5C, improving access to climate finance and winning greater recognition of the ocean-climate relationship; the same day Nauru and the Marshall Islands sign a trade and investment memorandum, Air Niugini restores direct Port Moresby to Tokyo flights after six years, and Papua New Guinea police arrest 27 men over the April Sambio village massacre in Morobe Province in which twelve people were killed
